description: HesabYar Phase 6 (MCP + AI access): MCP server on the official Python SDK v2 (MCP 2026-07-28, stdio + Streamable HTTP), the 14 read-only tools of spec §13.4 plus read-only tools for the Phase 5 reports (settlement, cheques, packaging, cashbox, cash forecast), resources + prompts, draft-only mutation tools, and MCP client management + conformance tests.

acceptanceCriteria: MCP server on the official Python MCP SDK v2, targeting the MCP 2026-07-28 specification; `mcp` 2.x pinned in uv.lock; Python 3.12 baseline
Transports: stdio (local developer) + Streamable HTTP (remote/production); NO new legacy HTTP+SSE implementation

Authentication + authorization: the same API-key + scope system as REST (hya_live_ keys, HMAC-SHA-256 + pepper); the company identity is always checked against the authenticated grant — a tool must NEVER accept a caller-provided company ID as proof of authorization; OAuth access tokens (if used) bound to the intended MCP resource/audience
Every MCP call is audit-logged (ai_access_audit: client, tool, company, scope, outcome, timestamp); no hidden chain-of-thought or provider secrets stored

The MCP server calls the SAME application query/command handlers as REST — no separate implementation of trial balance, tax calculation or posting for AI; no direct PostgreSQL access from any MCP tool (spec §0 rule 4); no API keys in tool arguments, URLs, logs or bundles
Protocol conformance + client-compatibility test harness in place (run in CI); server starts cleanly in both transports
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: MCP server core: SDK v2, MCP 2026-07-28, stdio + Streamable HTTP, REST-grade auth + scopes + audit, same application services as REST.
userStories.notes: Wave A (first — every other story builds on the server). Spec §13.2 + §13.3 + §13.8. The MCP process may share the HesabYar Python package and run as a separate process/container; the system stays a modular monolith.
userStories.title: MCP server core (SDK v2, transports, auth, audit)

acceptanceCriteria: All 14 read-only tools of spec §13.4, each calling the same application query service as the matching REST endpoint: list_companies (company:read), get_accounting_summary (reports:read), get_trial_balance (reports:read), get_general_ledger (ledger:read), get_balance_sheet (reports:read), get_income_statement (reports:read), get_cash_flow (reports:read), get_receivables_aging (reports:read), get_payables_aging (reports:read), get_bank_reconciliation_status (banking:read), get_tax_compliance_status (compliance:read), validate_financial_statement (standards:validate), explain_accounting_rule (standards:read), list_pending_review_items (workflow:read)
Tool arguments explicit and narrow: company, date range, report type, account filter, output detail — nothing else

Provenance on EVERY financial result (spec §13.7): company + period, currency + canonical unit (Rial), source engine + report type, generated timestamp + source-data freshness, snapshot/source reference, calculation/ruleset version, validation + incomplete-data warnings, and a clear statement that the model interprets supplied data and does not create authoritative financial facts
Amounts as integer Rial values or safe decimal strings — NEVER binary floating-point
Conformance test per tool (arguments, scopes, error shapes); equality test: the same report via MCP and via REST produces the same figures for the same company, date range and source snapshot
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: The 14 read-only tools of spec §13.4, with full §13.7 provenance and MCP-vs-REST equality.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-601 (server) + the Phase 5-6 report services (US-550). The equality test is a spec requirement (§13.3 + §19: 'A report requested from MCP and the dashboard must produce the same figures').
userStories.title: Read-only tools — the 14 of spec §13.4

acceptanceCriteria: Read-only MCP tools for the Phase 5 reports, same freshness + source metadata as §11.1: settlement status (tranches, expected vs received, variances), cheques (registry, due-soon, in-clearing aging, collateral), packaging + shipping costs, cash-box counts + variances, cash forecast (30/60/90/120-day, confirmed vs forecast)

Each tool reuses the existing application query service (US-521/US-531/US-515/US-516/US-553) — no duplicate logic; scopes match the REST endpoints (settlement:read, cheques:read, banking:read, reports:read as applicable)
MCP-vs-REST equality tests for the same data + period for every new tool
Provenance §13.7 on every result (same as US-602)
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Read-only MCP tools for the Phase 5 reports (settlement, cheques, packaging, cashbox, cash forecast).
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-601 + the Phase 5 report services. Phased design §1.3 phase 6: 'ابزارهای فقط‌خواندنی برای گزارش‌های جدید ... با همان فرادادهٔ تازگی و منبع §۱۱٫۱'.
userStories.title: Read-only tools — Phase 5 reports

acceptanceCriteria: Resources (all filtered by identity + company scope; NO unfiltered all-company resource): active chart-of-accounts metadata, available fiscal periods + company metadata, versioned standards summaries + verified source references, active tax-policy profile + applicability metadata, approved report snapshots with bounded access, integration + compliance status summaries

Prompts: monthly close review, explain unusual balance movement, summarize overdue receivables, review unreconciled bank activity, validate the financial statements for a period, compare month-over-month performance
Each prompt is a deterministic template over the read-only tools — the prompt never invents figures; every figure it cites comes from a tool call with provenance
Conformance tests for resources (scope filtering proven: a client scoped to company A cannot read company B's resource) and prompts (template renders + cites only tool-provided data)
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: MCP resources + prompts, all identity- and company-scoped.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-601 (+ US-602/US-603 for the data the prompts cite). Spec §13.6. The scope-filtering test is a SECURITY property — a cross-company read must fail closed.
userStories.title: MCP resources + prompts

acceptanceCriteria: Four draft-only tools (spec §13.5), exposed ONLY after the read-only tools are stable: prepare_journal_draft, prepare_invoice_draft, prepare_reconciliation_suggestions, prepare_tax_document_draft

Each tool creates a DRAFT object only and returns its ID + validation findings + the next human action; it must NEVER post the journal, finalize the invoice, approve a reconciliation, or submit anything to Moadian
Drafts go through the same validation + policy gate as dashboard-created drafts (draft by default, ADR 0003 decision 1); the draft is attributed to the MCP client in the audit log

NO approve_and_post tool in this release (spec §13.5: a later one would need a separately approved policy, explicit human confirmation, scoped identity, idempotency, complete audit logging — and a model's natural-language statement is NEVER approval)
Conformance tests per tool: draft created, nothing posted, findings + next action present, Moadian never touched
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Draft-only mutation tools — drafts only, never post/finalize/approve/submit.
userStories.notes: Wave C (after US-602/US-603 are stable — spec §13.5: 'After read-only MCP is stable'). Depends on US-601 + US-202 (journal drafts) + US-204 (invoices) + US-514 (reconciliation) + US-402/US-404 (tax/Moadian). The never-post guarantee is a SAFETY property — test it explicitly.
userStories.title: Draft-only mutation tools

acceptanceCriteria: MCP authorized-clients registry (mcp_authorized_clients): per-client scopes + company grants, key rotation + revocation, first-use secret shown exactly once (same rules as REST API keys: HMAC-SHA-256 + pepper, never in logs/bundles)
Admin UI (Persian RTL, VibeFarsi): list authorized MCP clients, create/revoke/rotate, audit log view (ai_access_audit: who called what, when, for which company, with what outcome)
Full protocol conformance suite in CI: every tool + resource + prompt against the MCP 2026-07-28 spec (client compatibility: at least the reference MCP client + one host-style client)

Operator docs: how to connect an AI client (stdio + Streamable HTTP), scope model, audit, revocation; security review of the MCP boundary documented (no direct DB access, no keys in arguments, OAuth audience binding, fail-closed scope checks)
Playwright: MCP client-management journey (create client → see it listed → revoke → audit shows the revocation); responsive checks at 360–390px
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: MCP client management (registry + admin UI + audit) + full conformance suite + operator docs.
userStories.notes: Wave C (last — needs the whole server). Depends on US-601–US-605. Frontend house rules in apps/admin/AGENTS.md apply. The conformance suite is the phase exit criterion (spec §17 phase 6 + phased design §1.3).
userStories.title: MCP client management + conformance + docs
